title: fix(app-shell,plugin-designer): the blank-target refusal banner describes a spec that is not installed (objectui#8897)
body:
Fixes #8897

The blank-target refusal banner told authors that `@objectstack/spec` **accepts** a whitespace-only relationship target, "so the PUT would succeed". Against the artifact this repo installs, it would not. Both metadata writers said it, word for word, and it is the text an author reads in the error banner.

⛔ **The guard's predicate is byte-identical.** objectui#8621 already ruled it stays for its own reason — it refuses at editor time, before the PUT, naming the field while it is still on screen. Only its stated *reason* was wrong.

## Clause-② declaration: **yes**

The diff moves a user-visible message string that ships in two published packages (`@object-ui/app-shell`, `@object-ui/plugin-designer`), so it is a change to an already-published **runtime payload** — the mechanical floor applies. No exported symbol is added and no published **type** face moves; the two travel independently and this is the payload half. Declared `yes` on the diff, not on the category.

## The installed pin, verified twice

    pnpm-lock.yaml            '@objectstack/spec@17.4.0':
                              '@objectstack/spec@17.4.0(ai@7.0.65(zod@4.4.3))'
    resolved tree             packages/app-shell/node_modules/@objectstack/spec/package.json -> 17.4.0

Parse behaviour re-measured on that artifact, in one run, with controls:

    FieldSchema  reference:'   '    success=false  codes=[custom]            paths=[reference]
    FieldSchema  reference:''       success=false  codes=[custom]            paths=[reference]
    FieldSchema  reference absent   success=false  codes=[custom]            paths=[reference]
    FieldSchema  reference:42       success=false  codes=[invalid_type]      paths=[reference]
    FieldSchema  referenceTo:'…'    success=false  codes=[unrecognized_keys] paths=[root]
    ObjectSchema fields.rel.reference:'   '  success=false  codes=[custom]   paths=[fields.rel.reference]

    CONTROLS, green in BOTH worlds (17.3.0 and 17.4.0):
    FieldSchema  reference:'account'     success=true
    FieldSchema  reference:' account '   success=true

⚠️ The two controls are chosen to be green at both pins. `''` and the absent case are **not** controls here — they are red at both pins by construction, which makes them a second subject, not a falsifier.

## ⭐ What the fired tripwire prescribed, and what it missed

The dispatch's instruction was to read the tripwire's own docblock and do what it prescribes rather than design a scheme. It turns out the tree carries **two** prescriptions, and only the first was executed.

**Prescription 1** — `MetadataService.specKeyReference.test.ts`, the tripwire row: *"the reading becomes `false` and nothing else here moves."* Honoured by objectui#8772, and scoped by its own wording to that file.

**Prescription 2** — both writers' guard docblocks, on the message itself: *"It retires with the pin bump, not with this note."* ⭐ Not executed. That sentence is the second half of the same closing scheme, and it names the pin bump as its trigger. This PR is that retirement.

The gap between them is recorded in the tripwire docblock now: `MetadataService.ts` was left untouched on the reasoning that the writer's refusal does not depend on the installed spec — true of the **predicate**, false of the **prose**. The lesson is written into the file so the next tripwire is not read the same way: a tripwire closes the reading it guards, not every statement that depended on the same fact, and the prose sites are the ones no assertion re-parses.

## The file surface I measured, against the claim comment's list

The claim comment declared six files. The measured surface is **seven**. Triage's own table lists six distinct files while its prose says five; that is a miscount in the summary line, not a missing site.

| file | in the claim? | what moved |
|---|---|---|
| `packages/plugin-designer/src/MetadataFieldsPage.tsx` | yes | banner text + guard docblock |
| `packages/plugin-designer/src/MetadataFieldsPage.specKeyReference.test.tsx` | yes | three stale claims, including a 17.2.0-era one triage could not see |
| `packages/app-shell/src/services/MetadataService.ts` | yes | banner text + guard docblock |
| `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/SchemaForm.groupSectionReachability-8725.test.tsx` | yes | two "installed 17.3.0" stamps |
| `packages/plugin-form/src/__tests__/formSectionGroupReference-7051.test.tsx` | yes | one stamp |
| `packages/types/src/field-types.ts` | yes | one stamp (the `domain:spec` mirror) |
| `packages/app-shell/src/services/MetadataService.specKeyReference.test.ts` | ⛔ **no** | the verbatim message pin, and the tripwire docblock's own account of what it closed |

⭐ The seventh is the one triage read as *already updated*. It is half-updated: it knew the pin was 17.4.0 and announced the skew closed, while still pinning the false sentence it was announcing about. Correcting the banner had to move it.

### Widening the probe, as instructed

Triage stated its probe matched the "what is installed" phrasings **containing the string 17.3.0**. Re-running by predicate (a version 17.0.x–17.3.x plus a present-tense installed-ness marker, excluding semver ranges and every `CHANGELOG`) surfaced a 17.2.0-era cohort triage was blind to by construction. Two of those sit inside this card's own family and moved here:

- `MetadataFieldsPage.specKeyReference.test.tsx` and `MetadataService.specKeyReference.test.ts`, both: *"pins at this repo's installed 17.2.0 — where the spec still accepts the draft"*. Doubly false now. Rewritten as the permanently-true statement it always was: the claim is about the PUT BODY, so it never depended on the pin in either direction.

The rest of that cohort — about **53 sites in 46 files across 13 packages**, on unrelated subjects — is measured and filed, not repaired here. See the notes section.

### The three "what changed" statements are not touched

`17.3.0 made reference a hard requirement`, `at 17.2.0 the requirement was prose only`, `17.3.0's #13632 refinement`, `silently at spec 17.2.0`. Verified mechanically: no removed line in this diff matches any of them, and no `CHANGELOG` file is in the diff.

⭐ The corrected banner deliberately says **"since 17.4.0"** rather than naming an installed pin. That converts a rotting "what is installed" claim into a permanently-true "when it changed" one, matching the form its three sibling branches already use. Re-stamping it 17.3.0 to 17.4.0 would have rotted again at the next bump.

## The expected cost, and where the card's premise did not hold

The dispatch warned the banner is asserted verbatim by pins in **both** writers' test files, and that correcting it would flip both red. ⚠️ Measured: **only one pin exists.**

`pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-designer/` — 18 files, 142 tests — stays fully green with that branch of the designer's message replaced by a marker sentence. Control: the identical mutation in `app-shell` turns exactly one test red, naming the row. Same mutation shape, same runner: the zero is a reading, not a blind spot.

⚠️ That gap bit inside this PR. An early draft wrote "This **page** refuses it first" in one copy and "This **writer** refuses it first" in the other; both originals said "writer". The whole designer suite stayed green and a hand `diff` of the two functions caught it. The two copies are word-for-word identical in the merged diff, verified that way.

⛔ The pin that does exist was re-pinned, never preserved. Its old assertions were `toMatch(/ACCEPTS this value/)` and `not.toMatch(/422/)`; both were assertions about a sentence the artifact contradicts.

## Ablation, both legs proven on disk

Run from the committed state, restored to `HEAD` and hash-verified, both legs:

    leg 1  app-shell banner reverted to the old sentence
           on disk: new text 0 / old text 1, blob c4a604b1 != HEAD abc64a49
           result: 1 failed | 17 passed — "expected … to match /TRIMMED value/"
           restored: hash == HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty

    leg 2  designer banner replaced by a marker sentence
           on disk: marker 1 / original 0, blob 8dd0f261 != HEAD 3662dc9f
           result: 18 files, 142 tests, ALL PASSED (no pin exists)
           control (unmutated): 18 files, 142 tests, all passed — identical
           restored: hash == HEAD blob, `git diff HEAD` empty

No build or `dist` is involved: both test files import the writer through a relative path inside its own package, so vitest reads `src` directly.

## Verification

All runs from the repo root, on head `2297caaba`.

| check | verdict |
|---|---|
| `vitest run packages/app-shell/ packages/plugin-form/ packages/types/` | ✅ 923 files, 10571 passed, 2 skipped |
| `vitest run packages/plugin-designer/` | ✅ 18 files, 142 passed |
| `turbo run type-check` (app-shell, plugin-designer, plugin-form, types) | ✅ 33 tasks |
| `eslint .` whole tree, `--format json` | ✅ 4688 files judged; **0 errors on all 7 changed files**; the 94 tree errors are pre-existing and name none of them |
| `check:designer-field-key-parity` | ✅ exit 0 |
| `check:spec-symbols` | ✅ exit 0 |
| `check:spec-floors` | ✅ exit 0 — after building; a bare run reports `no-artifact`, which is a prerequisite, not a verdict |
| `check:eager-closure` | ✅ exit 0 — after building; aggregate 3487.5 KB / 3512.7 KB. The banner is 10 bytes **shorter** per copy, so a byte ratchet cannot be breached by this diff |
| `check:control-bytes`, `check:comment-mask-corpus`, `check:i18n-keys`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:handler-key-reads` | ✅ all exit 0 |
| `check-changeset-presence` / `-no-major` / `-fixed` / `-overwrite` | ✅ all exit 0 |
| `check:governed-queue-guard` | ⚠️ NOT MEASURED locally — it reads a workflow event payload and refuses to exit 0 without one. Zero governed paths are in the diff by enumeration, so CI takes its cleared branch |

⚠️ **Honest limit on the typecheck.** The four test files in this diff are **not** type-checked: every affected package's `tsconfig.json` carries `exclude` entries for `**/*.test.ts`, `**/*.test.tsx` and `**/__tests__/**`. Typecheck covers the three source files only; the test files are covered by execution alone. That is the tree's pre-existing shape, not something this PR introduces, but it should not be read as "typecheck covered the diff".

## 验收备注 — measured, deliberately left to their own cards

Both are class (b) and both were deduplicated against the full open-issue list before filing (control: this card itself appears in that listing).

- **#8924** — the same rot in about **53 more sites, 46 files, 13 packages**, all naming an installed pin of 17.0.x–17.3.x. Out of scope here: each site states a different measured fact, and each needs its own re-measurement against 17.4.0 before its stamp can move. A bare string sweep is the wrong instrument and would plant fresh false premises. Two self-declared "interim, self-expiring" notes in that population have now outlived two pin bumps.
- **#8925** — the unpinned sibling banner described above, together with the docblock sentence "Both are pinned … so the copies cannot drift", which the ablation contradicts. Not repaired here because it needs new coverage, which is a new verification surface rather than a bounded in-place repair.
- noted, not filed: `.changeset/8621-retire-declared-divergence-note.md` states "this repo's pin is `@objectstack/spec` 17.3.0". Left alone on purpose — a pending changeset becomes a `CHANGELOG` entry verbatim, so it is a dated record of the change it describes, in the same category the fences protect. Whoever reads that release note should know it describes the tree as of objectui#8621. Carrier: the release-notes author.

## Channel note

`/search/issues` answers `403` in this session ("sessions are bound to their configured repositories"), and one targeted MCP `search_issues` returned zero for a query whose known positive is this very card — a dead instrument, not an empty population. Deduplication was therefore done on a single repo-scoped `GET /issues?state=open`, which returned the entire open population (82 issues) in one page and included the control.
